title: Five Lectures on Child Psychoanalysis
description: The introduction presents Éric Didier as a foremost specialist in child psychoanalysis internationally. It describes his early association with Lacan and his case-supervision training in Toronto as giving him a deep grounding in the work of his predecessors. With his characteristic rigour and pioneering approach, Didier delivered five lectures on child psychoanalysis at Sichuan University in Chengdu, China, in 2009. These lectures were warmly received in psychoanalytic circles; the introduction likens them to radiant beams of light and fresh, youthful springs that renew the energy to move beyond existing limits.

title: Masculine and Feminine
description: The book's introduction describes a Western context in which reliance on drug treatment has relegated psychoanalysis to a supplementary therapeutic role in the United States and Germany. In France, by contrast, it portrays psychoanalysis as deeply integrated into the country's cultural traditions, with an irreplaceable presence in literary criticism and even everyday thought. In China, psychoanalytic terminology remains relatively unfamiliar, both as a way of thinking and in daily life. Presented as a foundational account of psychoanalytic theory, the book had been published continuously in France for ten years. The French psychoanalyst Paul-Laurent Assoun develops a clear line of argument through the concept of bisexuality, which has been both generative and pivotal for psychoanalysis. From theoretical and clinical perspectives, he examines sexual difference and the ways in which the masculine and the feminine are inscribed in the subject.

It also offers a historical study of its development since the Renaissance, exploring how contemporary pornographic literature has been transformed by the combined influence of new technologies and feminism.

title: A Woman Alone
description: Centred on questions concerning women, this volume brings together essays and addresses published by the author between 1975 and 2006. Its three parts—Day by Day, Flesh and Spirit, and A Woman—draw on semiotics, psychoanalysis and anthropology, ranging across the French Enlightenment and Revolution to contemporary society. The book affirms the positive significance of women's agency and the maternal function, and advocates each woman's individual singularity and creativity.

title: Women and Mothers: The Question of the Feminine from Freud to Lacan
description: “What do women need?” Freud and Lacan offer different answers: for Freud, the response is to become an idealised mother; for Lacan, to become an object of desire. It is presented as a valuable resource for specialists in psychoanalysis and for readers seeking a more searching perspective on questions concerning women in China.

title: Chinese Conceptions of God and Spirits
description: The translation is based on a facsimile of the edition published in 1852. Legge's book is neither a scholarly monograph in the strict sense nor an academic article conforming to modern conventions; rather, it reorganises and brings together ideas and arguments developed in debate. Although the original is only 166 pages long, its range is extensive. It draws on the writings of European and American sinologists and Western philosophers, the Church Fathers and the Reformed tradition, the work of modern missionaries in the Far East, Indian religions, and Chinese Confucian, Buddhist and Daoist texts. Legge also occasionally introduces French and Latin, particularly in the semantic analysis of the second chapter, where he compares a variety of Western cultures and languages.

title: Lacan
description: Jacques Lacan is presented here as a psychologist and “France's Freud”. Drawing on the knowledge and techniques of linguistics, anthropology, philosophy and mathematics, he reinterpreted Freudian psychoanalysis and brought about major changes in its methodology and disciplinary character. The structuralist psychoanalysis he developed became closely identified with French psychoanalysis, and the Lacanian school became one of its most influential branches in France, with a substantial international reach. His distinctive theory is described as a bridge from structuralism to poststructuralism. It influenced major figures in postmodern thought and had a powerful impact on Western literature, culture, criticism, art and film in the later twentieth century.

description: Presented as a substantial contribution to contemporary European and North American literary geography, this book focuses on representations of place in contemporary literature. title: Berkeley’s World: An Examination of the Three Dialogues
description: This book presents Professor Tom Stoneham's interpretation of George Berkeley's Three Dialogues between Hylas and Philonous. Published in 1713, the Three Dialogues is a major philosophical work and a crucial stage in the development of Berkeley's idealism. Through dialogue, it debates the existence of matter and the nature of perception, setting out the position usually described as immaterialism or subjective idealism. Stoneham closely examines and critically interprets Berkeley's central philosophical ideas, locating the significance of the Three Dialogues in its contribution to debates about the nature of reality, perception and knowledge. Berkeley's idealism challenged the prevailing metaphysical positions of his time. His work also influenced later philosophers, including Immanuel Kant and George Santayana, who engaged with and responded to his ideas in their own philosophies.

The author relates the concept to three dimensions of the human psyche and explores how names affect the construction of identity.

title: Perception: An Essay on the Sensible
description: This book systematically challenges the reduction of perception in traditional philosophy to either sensation or intellect. Drawing on Husserl's account of adumbration, it presents perception as an original activity in which things are given through profiles: the presence of things themselves in their dynamic appearing. Barbaras argues that the perceiving subject should be understood as a living, embodied being in movement, and that the relation between perception and the world is fundamentally one of dynamic approach. Moving beyond the frameworks of Husserl and Merleau-Ponty, he develops the phenomenon of perception into a general ontology of sensible existence driven by desire. The book explores the ontological relations among life, body and world, opening a new path of thought for contemporary phenomenology.

title: Bergson on French Philosophy
description: This collection brings together a series of Bergson's essays and letters on French philosophy, the French spirit and French thinkers. For Bergson, the history of French philosophy since Descartes can be understood through two intersecting and mutually illuminating strands: an overt tradition of rationalism, represented by Descartes, Voltaire and Comte, and a less visible tradition centred on feeling, represented by Pascal, Rousseau and others. French philosophy has also consistently sought dialogue with science, attended to the literary qualities of philosophical expression, and aimed to speak in language that everyone can understand.
